On further review, I've gone from "ambivalent" to "strongly opposed." The repeal arguments are unconvincing and borderline dishonest.
> Observing that Articles 2 and 3 of GA#657 require member states to decriminalise the possession and personal use of all recreational drugs (with limited exceptions), even if the people who consume them thereby endanger their health and continued survival,
Is that so? Let's take a look:
> No member nation may prosecute, punish, or penalise any individual for their consumption of a psychoactive drug, so long as such consumption occurs in private and **does not pose a clear, specific, and imminent danger to the health or safety of other individuals.**
I think it just barely isn't a veracity violation (not all cases of "endanger their health" rise to "clear, specific, and imminent") but it could be an interesting challenge. Also, while I hate to invoke RL data, imposing harsh penalties for drug possession does not effectively stop people from using those drugs and American laws to that effect are some of the most provably racist we have.
> Noting that one of the target resolution's rationales for doing so is that policies of criminalisation have failed to "actually reduc[e] drug addiction and use," even though GA#643 "Reducing Addiction" already requires member states to provide education about and rehabilitation from drug addiction (and will continue to do so after the passage of this repeal), and
Criminalizing drugs is effective because rehab exists? Huh? What? You might as well say "I am Groot"

Ice pointed out that the repeal talks about self-harm while the target covers danger to others. I still think the argument is unconvincing even if it's fine on veracity. "While the target has exceptions for throwing people in jail for harming others, it doesn't let us throw people in jail for trying to harm themselves" is a weird point to make

I think that nations should have a right to outlaw drugs when those drugs are very clearly harmful. 

That criminalization is generally ineffective in real life is not, to me, a compelling reason to prevent them from trying.

Yet the target doesn’t prevent members from going after drug suppliers, banning the sale of drugs, or even confiscating drugs from users. All it unequivocally bans is taking punitive action against people merely for possessing drugs. You can still take the drugs away and throw the dealer in jail; you just can’t throw the user in jail. Try rehab instead
As I said, I hate RL justifications. It’s just that I hate missing an opportunity to use the “provably racist” line more
The repeal implying that members are forced to allow dangerous drugs on the streets is borderline dishonest and the Noting stuff is incoherent IMO
I think a stronger argument would be that the repeal’s exceptions actually undermine it and encourage people to get their drugs in underground ways
@Archon FOR per vote
